ACTION MINUTES
  OF THE APRIL 28, 2020 SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

NEXT RESOLUTION NO. R20-12

NEXT ORDINANCE NO. O20-745

CALL TO ORDER

A Special teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates City council via Zoom pursuant to
Executive Order N25-20 issued by Governor Gavin Newsom on March 12, 2020, was called to order
by Mayor McGowan at 3:34 pm, notice having been given with affidavit thereto on file. Members of
the public were provided with the following information to provide public input:

Join Zoom Meeting:
https://zoom.us/j/97713603586; or
via phone (669) 900-9128 Code: 977 1360 3586#

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE - The flag salute was waived.

ROLL CALL

Present via Zoom Teleconference: Councilmembers Davidson, Kao, Lozzi, Mayor Pro Tem
Kemps and Mayor McGowan

Also Present via Zoom Teleconference: City Manager Rukavina, Assistant to the City Manager
Bañales, City Attorney Hogin, Police Chief Dreiling, Planning Manager Rindge

APPROVAL OF AGENDA
 COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC –

Desiree Myers addressed the City Council

NEW BUSINESS:

  1.  City Council Workshop

  A. Review necessity for ad hoc and standing committees – review of purpose and scope
  B. Discuss issues surrounding a transactions and use tax and certificates of
  participation.

Acting City Manager Rukavina provided a report summarizing the procedures for a transactions and
use tax indicating the necessity to raise revenue from various sources. He explained a transactional
user tax would allow the city to capture a portion of internet sales and could generate $844,000 in
revenue.

The City Council discussed the issues and City Attorney Hogin advised that a use tax could be used
for general municipal services and was not a special tax; therefore, it would require only a simple
majority to pass.

The City Council concurred to look at this further and to invite two tax specialists to a meeting for
further discussion.

Acting City Manager Rukavina addressed the issuance of Certificates of Participation; how the funds
generated from Certificates of Participation became long-term debt and a liability on the City’s
General Fund. He also provided examples of Certificates of Participation being used for necessary
infrastructure or facilities; and could not be used for municipal services.

A brief discussion between the city Council and City Manager regarding Certificates of Participation.

Mark Young, a member of the Finance Advisory Committee confirmed the funds from the sale of
Certificates of Participation had limited uses and could not be used for operations. He also explained
the City did not have adequate sources of revenue to take on long-term debt.

Council concurred not to move forward with Certificates of Participation.

Thereafter, the City Council discussed the number of committees involved with the City; the
relevance of each committee; and whether council members should be actively involved with the
committees.

City Attorney Hogin counseled the Council regarding issues that could arise if a council member was
an active member of a committee.

Council concurred to discuss the issue of the committees at an upcoming meeting to determine what
committees were relevant and what committees were no longer required.
